To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
C3Ds show dual antibacterial/anti-biofilm activity in the absence and presence of β-lactamas.

(1) C3Ds can show both NO-donor and cephalosporine-like antibacterial activity, and (2) PYRRO-C4D, a C3D with a cephalosporinic acid backbone, is the first example of a compound showing dual-activity.

C3Ds, cephalosparin-NO-donors designed to selectively release NO following β -lactamase cleavage, also release NO following β- lactam-mediated reaction with transpeptidase/PBPs, the target of cephalospornins, and that this NO-release does not affect the antibacterial activity of C3Ds.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and development of NO donor prodrugs that selectively deliver NO to bacteria and that can also be triggered by β-lactam hydrolysis, a process that can occur in the presence of transpeptidase enzymes.
the development of cephalosparin-NO-donors as prodrugs for the selective delivery of NO to bacterial infection.
NO-donor prodrug design and the use of NO to modulate biofilms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PYRRO-C2D and PYRRO-C5D show NO-mediated activity against biofilm-forming Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes, respectively.
PYRRO-C-3D shows β- lactam-mediated activity against S. pneuomoniae biofilms, and the anti- pneumococcal action arises from the β-l actam component and not throug h NO-mediated effects.
the NO-donor prodrug, PYRRO-C2D, shows β-lactamate mediated activity against Streptosococus pneumoniae biofilm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
C3Ds are prodrugs designed for NO release in the presence of β-lactamas.
the C3D prodrugs can release NO and can also show direct cephalosporinic activity, but that the cephalosporic activity dominates over NO release.
C3Ds are a promising novel class of antibiotics that are able to deliver NO at the infection site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
C3Ds show dual-activity, combining NO-mediated anti-bacterial effects with intrinsic β-lactam antibacterial activity.
C3Ds show potential as anti-biofilm agents and can also be used to treat infections caused by β-lactamase negative bacteria.
NO-donor prodrug cephalosporines can show dual-activity as NO-releasing agents and β-lactamase-independent cephalosporine derivatives.
